questions.questionText: Two trains 150 m and 300 m long cross a pole in 5 seconds and 20 seconds respectively. If they run in opposite directions, how many seconds will they take to cross each other?
questions.explanation: Speeds: 150/5 = 30 m/s and 300/20 = 15 m/s. Relative speed = 45 m/s. Time = 450/45 = 10 seconds.
questions.shortcut: Find each speed from its pole crossing, then use the relative speed.

questions.questionText: Two trains 120 m and 180 m long run in opposite directions. The first runs at 36 km/h and they cross each other in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the second train in km/h?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 300/12 = 25 m/s = 90 km/h. Second = 90 - 36 = 54 km/h.
questions.shortcut: Total distance / time gives the relative speed; subtract the known speed.

questions.questionText: A train running at 108 km/h crosses a pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: Speed = 108 km/h = 108 x 5/18 = 30 m/s. Length = 30 x 15 = 450 metres.
questions.shortcut: Convert km/h to m/s (x 5/18); length = speed x time.

questions.questionText: A 200 m long train running at 63 km/h passes a slower train running at 45 km/h in the same direction in 100 seconds. What is the length of the slower train?
questions.explanation: Distance covered = 5 x 100 = 500 m = 200 + length. Slower train = 300 m.
questions.shortcut: Distance = relative speed x time; subtract the known length.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long running at 90 km/h crosses a platform in 40 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation: Distance covered = 25 x 40 = 1000 m. Platform = 1000 - 120 = 880 metres.
questions.shortcut: Platform length = (speed x time) - train length.

questions.questionText: A train passes two men walking in the same direction at 18 km/h and 24 km/h in 15 seconds and 18 seconds respectively. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation: Let the train's speed be s. L = (s - 18)(5/18)(15) = (s - 24)(5/18)(18). Solving gives s = 54 km/h (and L = 150 m).
questions.shortcut: Equate the length from both passes and solve for the speed.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long runs at 81 km/h. In how many seconds will it pass a man walking at 9 km/h in the same direction?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 81 - 9 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Time = 200/20 = 10 seconds.
questions.shortcut: Same direction: speeds subtract. The train must cover only its own length.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform 190 m long in 36 seconds and another platform 230 m long in 40 seconds. What is the speed of the train in m/s?
questions.explanation: The extra distance 230 - 190 = 40 m takes 40 - 36 = 4 s. Speed = 40/4 = 10 m/s.
questions.shortcut: Difference in platform lengths / difference in times = speed.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform 280 m long in 20 seconds and another platform 380 m long in 24 seconds. What is the speed of the train in m/s?
questions.explanation: The extra distance 380 - 280 = 100 m takes 24 - 20 = 4 s. Speed = 100/4 = 25 m/s.
questions.shortcut: Difference in platform lengths / difference in times = speed.
